  "description": "Expanded Series Bible III #34 Turned Into a Woman: adult {{user}} is physically transformed into an adult female body by a curse, potion, accident, technology or unexplained event while keeping his memories, personality and agency. The engine varies the cause, pace, reversibility, witnesses, confidants and the practical fallout for identity documents, work, housing and relationships.",

    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible III",

  "summary": "{{user}} begins as an adult man and, through an unusual event or process — a curse, potion, mislabelled pill, experimental medication, laboratory accident, artefact, wish or unexplained phenomenon — is physically transformed into an adult female body while retaining his existing memories, personality, identity, preferences and agency. The engine is the collision between an unchanged self and a changed body: who saw it, who believes him, who he turns to, how work, university, housing, documents and recognition are affected, and whether the change is temporary, reversible, uncertain or permanent. The cause never dictates his reaction; embracing, rejecting, renegotiating or simply coping with the new body are all open.",
  "core_premise": "An adult man's body is transformed into an adult female body by an external cause, without rewriting his mind. {{user}} keeps his memories, personality, identity, orientation, preferences and decision-making power; the transformation changes anatomy, not who he is. Cards vary the cause and its rules, the pace (instant or gradual), the prognosis (temporary, reversible, uncertain or permanent), who witnessed the event, who {{user}} confides in or seeks help from, and how the practical world responds — identity documents, employment, university enrolment, housing, health care and being recognised by people who knew him before. Nothing about the change predetermines femininity, submissiveness, changed attraction, embarrassment, acceptance or rejection; those remain {{user}}'s open choices.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult transformation-drama opening. Establish who {{user}} was before the change — name, occupation or study, living situation and one or two relationships that matter — then the cause and its rules: what happened, whether it was instant or gradual, whether anyone witnessed it, and what is known or unknown about reversal. Begin at or just after the moment the change becomes undeniable, with the first practical problem already pressing (a mirror, a locked phone, a landlord's knock, a colleague's call, a doctor's appointment). Introduce at least one adult {{char}} with her own life, motives and limits — witness, confidante, ex-partner, colleague, specialist, stranger or the person responsible — who can help, hinder, exploit or simply misunderstand. Do not write {{user}}'s reaction, feelings, decisions or future; leave how he handles the body, the disclosure and the search for answers entirely open.",
  "core_variables": [
    "The cause: curse, potion, mislabelled pill, experimental medication, fictional illness, infection, laboratory accident, advanced technology, artefact, magic, wish or unexplained event.",
    "Whether the transformation is instant or gradual, and if gradual, over what timescale and with what milestones.",
    "The prognosis: temporary with a known endpoint, reversible with effort or cost, genuinely uncertain, or permanent from the start.",
    "Whether anyone witnessed the transformation, and whether witnesses believe what they saw.",
    "Who {{user}} turns to for help: friend, ex-partner, colleague, sibling, doctor, researcher, stranger, rival or the person who caused it.",
    "Who believes {{user}}'s identity claim, who doubts it, and what proof is possible.",
    "How identity documents, banking, work, university, housing, leases and official records are affected.",
    "How health care and the transformed body's physiology are handled, defined only where the scenario requires it.",
    "Whether the person or force responsible is known, remorseful, indifferent, hidden or actively interfering.",
    "How people who knew {{user}} before — family, friends, partners, coworkers — react to the changed body.",
    "Whether {{user}} hides the change, presents a new identity, or discloses the truth, and to whom first.",
    "The setting's register: mundane modern, near-future science, fantasy, historical or deliberately unexplained.",
    "What the transformation's rules forbid or permit, and what a cure or reversal would actually cost.",
    "Whether {{char}} enters before, during or after the change, and what she independently wants from the situation.",
    "How daily logistics — clothes, voice, name, pronouns, gym, toilets, dating profiles — are negotiated without scripting {{user}}'s choices.",
    "Whether the change stays stable, recurs, progresses or carries conditions {{user}} must manage."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, orientation, identity conclusions, future behaviour or reaction to the new body.",
    "Physical transformation does not automatically rewrite {{user}} mentally. Do not assume femininity, submissiveness, attraction to men, fashion interest, embarrassment, changed orientation or acceptance/rejection of the new body.",
    "Menstruation, fertility and pregnancy capability should be defined only when the generated body's physiology requires it, never as automatic texture.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults, including {{user}} before and after the change.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Whether {{user}} seeks reversal, adapts, discloses, hides, relocates or redefines himself remains roleplay space.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: a {{char}} may assume {{user}} is coping well, secretly thrilled, doomed or faking, but those assumptions are not narrator-endorsed facts.",
    "Transformation does not remove {{user}}'s autonomy: others may not expose, photograph, touch, examine or use the new body without consent, regardless of who caused the change.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase personality: {{char}} remains a full person with occupation, interests, limits and judgement outside her role in the transformation.",
    "The cause does not dictate morality: magic, science or accident are not punishments for {{user}}'s character, and the transformed state is not inherently humiliation, upgrade or comeuppance.",
    "Being transformed is not consent: curiosity, medical interest or attraction from others never grants access to {{user}}'s body, records or story.",
    "Whoever caused the transformation — curse-caster, negligent lab, well-meaning friend — may have motives, but their rationalisations are beliefs, not ground truth about what {{user}} needed or deserved.",
    "Do not force romance into the premise. Friendship, practical partnership, medical drama, comedy, unresolved tension or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Vary reversibility honestly: some cards offer a clear cure path with costs, some an uncertain one, some none; do not hint at guaranteed reversal the premise does not establish.",
    "Keep practical consequences real: documents, work, housing, health access and recognition carry logistics that generate scenes without needing melodrama.",
    "Adult {{char}} should have independent stakes — her own goals, history and limits — rather than existing solely as helper, temptress or authority figure.",
    "Do not treat the female body as a downgrade, upgrade, joke or fetish object by default; the frame stays non-graphic and the meaning belongs to {{user}}.",
    "If {{user}} chooses to present as a new person, establish what that identity can and cannot do; forged or borrowed identities have failure points.",
    "Witnesses and confidants can misread the situation dramatically and sincerely; let misunderstandings be plausible rather than cartoonish.",
    "Overlap boundary: distinct from We Swapped Bodies (nobody else occupies {{user}}'s original body), from Reborn as a Woman (no death or new life), and from We Both Changed ({{char}} is not transformed too).",
    "Preserve the fixed engine — an adult man's body changed to an adult female body with his mind intact — while varying everything around it.",
    "Open at a playable moment: the morning after, the mirror, the witness's knock, the clinic door, the second dose decision — not a completed arc.",
    "Keep all transformation and intimacy non-graphic; the card sells the situation's human consequences, not anatomical detail."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants, including {{user}} before and after the transformation, are adults.",
    "The transformation changes {{user}}'s body, never his memories, personality, agency or decision-making power.",
    "No predetermination of {{user}}'s orientation, gender identity conclusions, comfort, embarrassment or acceptance.",
    "Others' assumptions about the new body or about who {{user}} now 'must' be are beliefs, not objective truth.",
    "Consent is activity-specific: looking, treating, housing or helping does not imply touching, photographing or intimacy.",
    "The changed body is not public property; medical curiosity, magic rules or an accidental cause grant no access rights.",
    "Whoever caused the change owes honesty when confronted but retains their own perspective; blame and forgiveness stay open.",
    "No compulsory humiliation, sexualisation, romance, pregnancy, permanent loss or guaranteed cure as a default outcome.",
    "{{char}} keeps her own life, interests and boundaries beyond the transformation plot.",
    "Practical matters — documents, work, housing, health — are handled as adult logistics, not as traps forcing intimacy.",
    "Keep the premise non-graphic; foreground identity, trust and daily consequences over anatomy.",
    "Friendship, rivalry, professional help, comedy and unresolved tension are valid alongside or instead of romance."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "Cause: curse, potion, mislabelled pill, experimental medication, fictional illness, infection, laboratory accident, advanced technology, artefact, magic, wish or unexplained event.",
    "Pace: instant overnight change, hours-long shift, weeks of gradual transformation, or episodic progression.",
    "Prognosis: temporary with a known endpoint, reversible at a cost, uncertain, or permanent from the first scene.",
    "Witnesses: nobody, one trusted friend, a stranger, a crowd, the person responsible, or authorities.",
    "First confidant: best friend, ex-partner, sibling, colleague, doctor, researcher, online stranger, rival or the culprit.",
    "Credibility: everyone believes {{user}}, nobody does, proof is possible, or proof is dangerous.",
    "Practical fallout focus: documents and banking, work, university, housing and lease, health care, family recognition.",
    "Culprit's stance: unknown, remorseful and helping, indifferent, hidden and observing, or actively interfering.",
    "Setting register: mundane modern, near-future science, urban fantasy, historical or deliberately unexplained.",
    "{{char}}'s role: witness, helper, medical or magical specialist, person responsible, new acquaintance, old flame, suspicious official.",
    "{{char}}'s motive: guilt, scientific curiosity, protection, attraction, opportunity, duty, friendship or self-interest.",
    "{{user}}'s presentation strategy: hide the change, new identity, partial disclosure, full disclosure — left open, not fixed.",
    "Tone: drama, comedy of errors, quiet slice-of-life, mystery about the cause, medical or magical procedural.",

    "How stable the change is: fixed, recurring, conditional, slowly progressing or tied to the cause's unfinished business."

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Turned Into a Woman. Adult {{user}}, a man, is physically transformed into an adult female body by a curse, potion, mislabelled pill, experimental medication, fictional illness, laboratory accident, advanced technology, artefact, literally granted wish or unexplained event, while keeping his memories, personality, identity and agency. Vary the cause and its rules, instant versus gradual pace, temporary, reversible, uncertain or permanent prognosis, witnesses and who believes him, the first confidant, and the practical fallout across documents, work, university, housing and health. Include an adult {{char}} with independent motives. Never assume the change makes him feminine, submissive, attracted to men, embarrassed or accepting, and never script his decisions or identity conclusions. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and {{user}}'s choices remain open. Open at a playable moment and leave every outcome unwritten."
